segments.title: Chương 61: 0061【Truyền thông bùng nổ】
segments.content:
When it came to sincerity, no one could beat Beijing Normal University.

In the final stretch of the recruitment battle, Director Yan made a multitude of promises.

As long as Chen Guiliang enrolled, he could choose any professor he wanted, and his path to a master's or doctorate would be a green light all the way.

Not to mention other things like joining the Party, the student union, or getting scholarships.

Why was this so?

It had to do with Beijing Normal University's development strategy.

Last year, BNU officially established its College of Literature, built upon the foundation of its Chinese department, and ranked third in the nation.

From then on, it went on a frenzy, recruiting famous scholars as professors and scouting for promising students everywhere. Last year, the entire university had only 18 discretionary admission slots, and 7 of them went directly to first-prize winners of the New Concept Writing Competition.

Twenty years later, BNU's Chinese department would become number one in the country!

Chen Guiliang felt Beijing Normal University's sincerity, but he didn't agree immediately.

Because he also felt the sincerity of Peking University, Fudan University, Xiamen University, and East China Normal University…

In any case, the discretionary admission exams were not until March, still a long way off. He would decide after the New Year.

Chen Guiliang bowed respectfully in different directions to the admissions officers, "Thank you very much, esteemed leaders, for your consideration. I'm incredibly excited right now and can't think straight. I'd like to go back and discuss this with my teachers and parents."

Hearing this, Director Wang from Fudan began to worry.

If the decision were to be made in the next two days, Fudan was undoubtedly the most suitable choice for Chen Guiliang.

But if it dragged on for another month or two, after Tsinghua and Peking University held their meetings and were willing to offer Chen Guiliang special admission, then Fudan would lose its advantage.

Director Wang stared at Chen Guiliang for a long while, thinking: Is this kid just trying to stall for time?

Chen Guiliang left his phone number with every university, not even leaving out a few art schools, and then bowed again. "I won't disturb the other students' inquiries any longer. I'll head back to my room to call my family first."

With that, Chen Guiliang bowed a third time before leaving, leaving the group of admissions officers staring at each other.

Director Wang from Tsinghua chuckled and cursed, "Clever little rascal."

Director Wang was the happiest one. He didn't even have a slot to offer and couldn't make any promises. Stalling for time was most advantageous for Tsinghua!

After all the other award winners had finished their consultations, Minister Cheng of Peking University found Cao Wenxuan and gave him a rough account of the evening's events.

Cao Wenxuan said, "This Chen Guiliang is quite shrewd. I was afraid he'd be snatched away tonight. Hearing you describe BNU's stance, they probably wanted to sign a direct admission contract on the spot. But he didn't agree to anyone, nor did he refuse anyone. It's clear he wants to wait for the highest bidder."

"So mature and smooth for someone so young," Minister Cheng said with a laugh.

Cao Wenxuan said, "Sprout will give him the greatest possible publicity. He'll be famous throughout the country, and with positive press at that. Under these circumstances, Tsinghua's meeting will definitely approve it! Our, Peking University's, rival isn't Fudan, it's Tsinghua."

Minister Cheng said, "We need to go back and fight for him too, and try to give him the most generous offer possible. I can just about accept it if Fudan gets him, but he absolutely cannot be snatched away by Tsinghua."

They could tolerate anyone else, but not that Wudaokou Vocational School across the street.

Chen Guiliang returned to his room, but of course, he didn't call anyone.

He sat on the edge of the bed and watched TV.

Before long, the door opened, and his temporary roommate, Luo Jin, returned.

Luo Jin looked a bit awkward because a group of people was following behind him.

"Chen Guiliang, what's your QQ number? Do you have a cell phone?"

"Damn, brother, you're awesome!"

"Classmate Chen, which university are you planning to attend? Each school only has so many special admission slots. If you tell me, I can steer clear."

"Hey handsome, did you really write a piece in classical Chinese?"

"Hello, Chen Guiliang, I'm from Mianzhou. We're fellow Sichuanese."

"..."

Twenty to thirty people swarmed in. Not only did the first-prize winners from Group A show up, but even the younger students from Group B came to join the fun.

The room was already too crowded, and some people were standing outside the door.

There was no way he could kick them out. Chen Guiliang greeted them enthusiastically, "Hello everyone, come on in and watch TV. My QQ number is 25XX08."

"Wow, a six-digit premium QQ number!" several people exclaimed in awe.

This QQ number had been registered by his cousin's husband.

Back then, Feng Tao had registered three: one for himself, one for his girlfriend, and one he gave to Chen Guiliang.

Everyone took down the QQ number, and the room became noisy again.

Chen Guiliang remained silent. He waited until they had mostly settled down before continuing, "So many people are asking questions, I can't hear clearly. How about we go one by one?"

"Let me go first!"

A girl raised her hand first.

Chen Guiliang smiled. "Hello."

The girl was delighted and shook his hand. "My name is Li Jing, from Huzhou Deqing No. 3 Middle School. Do you know Guo Xiaosi?"

This question made everyone keel over.

Chen Guiliang said, "I've seen him at school. I know him, but he doesn't know me."

Another boy raised his hand. "I'm Liu Lin from Qilu Experimental Middle School. Can you tell us more about your essay?"

Chen Guiliang said, "I wrote a classical-style poem and a preface for it. You should all be able to see it tomorrow."

As they were speaking, a few more people rushed in from outside. They were non-first-prize winners who had heard the news.

"Who is your favorite Chinese author?"

"Lu Xun."

"Among those still living."

"Wang Meng."

"And from abroad?"

"Uh, let's stick to one question per person. For foreign authors, I like Victor Hugo."

"Which university's discretionary admission program are you planning to apply for?"

"I'm not sure yet."

"You're definitely going to be famous this time. Will you write a book for publication?"

"It's possible."

"A novel or a collection of essays?"

"One question per person."

"..."

Even after everyone had asked their questions, they lingered, continuing to chat among themselves. And they weren't chatting with Chen Guiliang, but had broken off into small groups.

They exchanged QQ numbers, and after literature, they talked about movies; after movies, they talked about music.

Some of the boys were even talking about video games!

The place had practically become a New Concept social center.

During the chat, people kept leaving, and new people, having heard the news, kept arriving.

Chen Guiliang sighed helplessly. Luo Jin, sitting on the bed, shrugged and threw his hands up.

Hong Kong has a Wen Wei Po, and so does Shanghai.

The two newspapers shared the same roots.

Dong Hongkang was the supplementary editor for Shanghai's Wen Wei Po. He hadn't planned on covering the New Concept Writing Competition.

The reason was simple: he looked down on it!

Just a bunch of kids' essays.

Last night, Zhao Changtian, the editor-in-chief of Sprout, had called him and read a preface to him right over the phone. He had added, "The main poem is even more brilliant. We're holding a seminar tomorrow. Editor Dong, would you care to join us?"

So he came.

"Brother Dong, what brings you here too?"

Just as Dong Hongkang got out of the car at the hotel, he heard someone calling from behind. He turned to see it was Feng Wenya, a female reporter from the Oriental Morning Post.

The two newspapers both belonged to the Shanghai United Media Group.

But their positioning was different; one was high-end and sophisticated, the other was more down-to-earth.

Today, they had both come.

"It's Xiao Feng," Dong Hongkang smiled. "Chief Editor Zhao called me personally. I had to give him some face."

Feng Wenya asked, "Brother Dong, did you hear a preface?"

Dong Hongkang nodded. "I was drawn in by the last two paragraphs of the preface. If it was truly written by a high school student, and the main poem maintains that level, then he is definitely a rare literary prodigy."

"I heard several major universities were fighting over him last night," Feng Wenya said with a smile.

Dong Hongkang said, "If I were in charge of admissions, I'd be fighting for him too."

The two walked into the hotel lobby, chatting and laughing. Feng Wenya suddenly pointed ahead. "That's the Shanghai correspondent for Southern Weekly."

Dong Hongkang pursed his lips. "Sprout is really putting a lot of effort into promotion this time."

"It's been on a downturn for several years. It's rare for them to get another good piece of writing, so of course they're going to hype it up as much as possible," Feng Wenya said.

"Good morning, you two!"

A staff member from Sprout came up to greet them. After a few pleasantries, they began handing out copies of the essay.

Dozens of copies had been printed last night!

Dong Hongkang read it carefully, going through it twice. "Was this really written by a high school student?"

"It certainly was."

"Was there a separate make-up exam?"

"Make-up exams were banned long ago. The New Concept Competition is very official now. The essay prompts from the organizing committee are sealed until the semi-finals begin. The chairman of the committee is the vice president of Peking University. Of the other nine members, one is the dean of Tsinghua, and the other eight are all vice presidents. It's absolutely impossible for the topic to be leaked in advance!"

"Incredible!"

"Please wait upstairs, you two."

When they went upstairs, they were surprised. Whoa, there were thirty to forty media outlets present.

These journalists, regardless of their usual relationships, were all chatting and laughing with one another.

The topic of discussion, naturally, was that essay.

Before long, the members of the judging committee and the award-winning students entered the room.

There were too many winners for the second prize and below, so their certificates weren't presented publicly but were given out privately.

The first to go on stage to receive their awards were the first-prize winners of Group B.

They stood in two rows, holding their certificates to their chests. After a photo was taken, they quickly left the stage. There wasn't even a segment for acceptance speeches.

Next up were the first-prize winners of Group A.

"Chen Guiliang, you stand in the middle!" Hu Weishi ran over to adjust their positions.

With his certificate held high, Chen Daxia made his C-position debut.

"Li Haiyang, you stand next to Chen Guiliang."

Li Haiyang walked over and said in a low voice, "I got your QQ last night. Let's chat online when you have time. By the way, my screen name on the Sprout forum is 'Dead Fatty'."

Chen Guiliang smiled. "Then I've seen you before. You sure tore into Guo Xiaosi pretty harshly."

Chen Guiliang had seen "Dead Fatty" when he was stirring up trouble on the forums. The guy had relentlessly flamed Chen Guiliang's alternate account at the time.

"Uh, about that..." Li Haiyang thought quickly. "It was probably my cousin secretly using my forum account. Don't mention this to Guo Xiaosi."

"No problem."

"Thanks."

The thirty to forty media outlets below the stage were all focusing their attention on Chen Guiliang.

Sprout wanted to make big news, and for the sake of sales, the media was happy to cooperate.

However, whether to praise or criticize would depend on the specific circumstances.

Unanimous praise wouldn't hold public attention for long.

There needed to be some criticism.

A mix of praise and criticism, a back and forth—a war of words would be much more entertaining to watch!

(Thanks to Boss Ruxuan for the Alliance Leader tip.)

(Offering up a book: Reborn in a New Life, I Became a God with One Book. Old Wang ran around as an extra in the book for many chapters, responsible for shouting '666' at the protagonist.)
